text:
[LDET.1.11] **The guarantee is for an artefact that does not lie.** A run in
which evaluating an expression raises an `EngineError` — a value contradicting
the type the artefact declared for it ([IRET.9.6]) — is outside [LDET.1.1]. Two
conforming runtimes may then differ in whether they meet the error at all: one
may reject a fact on a comparison that never inspects the lie, where another
evaluates the lying operand and halts the tier. That error ends the trace, as
every halting fault does ([LFST.9.2.1]); what precedes it stays comparable.

alloy.name: iret_9_6__honest
alloy.note: The artefact did not lie: no conjunct yields an EngineError, the third arm of [IRET.9.6]. The determinism guarantee is scoped to such runs ([LDET.1.11]).

alloy.name: iret_9_6__v5_lie_breaks_hoisting
alloy.note: WHY THE ARTEFACT MUST NOT LIE: a hoisted conjunct over a value the artefact lied about raises its EngineError alone and blocks the `no` pattern, where the whole `where` is false.

alloy.name: rlow_5_5__v5_hoist_sound
alloy.note: HOISTING AND PROBING ARE SOUND for an artefact that does not lie: filters on decided conjuncts leave the decision of a positive and of a `no` pattern, and the record, unchanged. Admitting a nullable filter breaks it (TEETH). V5 as stated by [LNUL.4.2] and [IRET.9.5]: a false decides wherever it stands; otherwise the faults resolve by kind, then by the fields of the record (T2I); the evaluation order is free.

idris.name: rlow_5_5__faulting_filter_differs
idris.note: WHY NO FAULT: a filter raising an EngineError -- an artefact that lied, [IRET.9.6] -- raises it alone and blocks a `no` pattern where the `where` is false. So two engines may differ on an artefact that lies, which is why [LDET.1.11] scopes the guarantee to one that does not.
